cands.bio: Retired U.S. Army colonel with 26 years of service, including command of a battalion task force in Iraq. Founded and sold a defense and cyber consulting firm. Served as acting Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy in 2025. Republican nominee for NC-1 in 2024 and 2026.

controversies.text: In August 2026, the prediction market Kalshi fined her $2,589.96 and suspended her for three years. She had bet less than $1,000 on her own House race, and Kalshi's rules bar candidates from trading on their own races. She said: "It was a dumb mistake, and as soon as I learned there was an issue, I worked to make it right."

She was charged with DUI in Richmond County, Georgia, on Aug. 8, 2017. On Oct. 8, 2019, she pleaded guilty to reckless driving and was ordered to pay a $500 fine. Two other charges were dropped. Her campaign said she "made a mistake which she deeply regrets."

endorsements.text: Endorsed by President Donald Trump for the 2026 race.
Endorsed in 2024 by Donald Trump and the Congressional Leadership Fund.
Endorsed in 2026 by the Leading the Future super PAC, which is backed by Andreessen Horowitz and OpenAI, per Wikipedia.

cands.gaps: She has never held elected office, so there are no legislative votes or official actions to report. We found no documented statements from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, police pay, school choice or teacher pay. Her campaign site says she wants to cut regulations and 'unleash American energy to power our tech sector' and to lead on AI, but it does not mention data centers. Her pro-life position is known only from a one-line 2024 campaign priority. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. We found no documented foreign ties.

cands.bio: Democrat and former Air Force captain who has represented North Carolina's 1st District in the U.S. House since 2023. Former mayor of Snow Hill (from 2001) and state senator for District 5 (2009–2011, 2013–2023). Taught aerospace studies at East Carolina University.
cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from Don Davis on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, gun policy, abortion, policing, school choice or teacher pay. We found no documented controversies. We could not confirm which years of his childhood were spent in North Carolina and which in Texas. His record was read from a single encyclopedia-style page, not from primary government records or news reports.
